evals.prompt: Draw the full architecture of our commerce platform so new engineers can see how everything connects. Clients: Web Storefront (Next.js), iOS App, Android App, Admin Console. Edge: Cloudflare CDN, WAF, API Gateway (Kong). Identity domain: Auth Service, User Profile Service, Session Store (Redis). Catalog domain: Catalog Service, Search Service, Elasticsearch, Pricing Service, Catalog DB (PostgreSQL). Orders domain: Cart Service, Checkout Service, Order Service, Orders DB (PostgreSQL), Order Events (Kafka topic). Payments domain: Payment Service, Fraud Scoring, Stripe (external), Ledger DB. Fulfilment domain: Inventory Service, Warehouse Service, Shipping Service, ShipStation (external), Inventory DB. Notifications: Notification Service, SendGrid (external), Twilio (external). Analytics: Event Collector, Snowflake, dbt Transformations, Power BI. Platform: Kubernetes cluster boundary around all internal services, Vault for secrets, Datadog for observability. Flows: clients go through CDN -> WAF -> API Gateway; the gateway authenticates against Auth Service and routes to Catalog, Search, Cart, Checkout, Order and User Profile; Checkout calls Pricing, Inventory, Payment and then Order Service; Payment calls Fraud Scoring and Stripe and writes the Ledger DB; Order Service writes Orders DB and publishes to Order Events; Inventory, Warehouse, Notification and Event Collector consume Order Events; Warehouse calls Shipping which calls ShipStation; Notification calls SendGrid and Twilio; Event Collector loads Snowflake, dbt transforms it, Power BI reads it; all services pull secrets from Vault and ship telemetry to Datadog. Save the HTML to the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: One standalone HTML architecture diagram containing every named component and the described flows, on the infinite canvas.

evals.prompt: I need a workflow diagram of our purchase-to-pay process in Business Central for the controller. Lanes: Requester, Department Manager, Purchasing, Receiving, Accounts Payable, Treasury, and an Exceptions lane. Steps in order: Requester creates Purchase Requisition -> Department Manager reviews budget -> (over $10k goes to CFO Approval in the manager lane, otherwise straight on) -> Purchasing selects vendor -> Purchasing creates Purchase Order in BC -> Vendor acknowledges PO -> Receiving receives goods -> Receiving posts Warehouse Receipt -> AP receives vendor invoice (email intake) -> AP runs OCR capture -> AP performs three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice) -> AP posts Purchase Invoice -> Treasury builds payment proposal -> Treasury approves payment run -> Treasury exports bank file -> Bank confirms payment -> AP reconciles vendor ledger. Exceptions: budget rejected returns to the Requester; quantity mismatch at three-way match goes to 'Resolve receiving discrepancy' and back to three-way match; price variance goes to 'Purchasing price review' and back to the match; failed bank file goes to 'Fix payment rejection' and back to the export. Don't leave steps out - the auditors will compare it to the SOP. Save the HTML to the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: One standalone HTML workflow diagram with all 17 main steps plus the four exception paths, on the infinite canvas.

evals.prompt: Map the data lineage for Rico's reporting stack as a data flow diagram. Sources: NetSuite (sales orders, invoices, inventory), ClickUp (tasks, time entries), Shopify (web orders), SQL Server ERP archive, and a vendor price list that arrives as CSV over SFTP. Ingestion: a NetSuite SuiteTalk extractor, a ClickUp API poller, a Shopify webhook receiver and an SFTP file watcher all publish to RabbitMQ; the SQL Server archive is read by a nightly SSIS package. Landing: RabbitMQ consumers write raw JSON to a Bronze landing zone in Azure Data Lake; SSIS writes to the same Bronze zone. Staging: a JSON flattener produces Silver tables for orders, invoices, inventory, tasks, time entries and price lists. Conformance: customer master match (MDM), item master match (MDM), and a currency conversion step. Warehouse: Gold star schema in Azure SQL with FactSales, FactInventory, FactLabor, DimCustomer, DimItem, DimDate. Semantic layer: a Power BI dataset with sales, inventory and labor models. Consumption: Executive Sales dashboard, Inventory Aging report, Labor Utilization report, and a finance Excel export. Mark customer data as PII wherever it moves, and show data quality checks between Silver and Gold that quarantine bad rows to a Rejects table. Save the HTML to the outputs folder.
evals.expected_output: One standalone HTML dataflow diagram covering every source, step, table and report named, on the infinite canvas.
